articleMarkdown:
# Six of Pentacles: Giving with Clear Terms

Let resources reach where they are needed, while noticing who decides their distribution.

Keywords: Giving · Receiving · Distribution

Upright at a glance: Offer or accept practical support, with its purpose and limits made clear.

Reversed at a glance: Help may carry hidden conditions, or contributions and decision-making power may remain unequal.

The Six of Pentacles contains outstretched hands and a set of scales held by someone else. It shows generosity alongside differences in position: someone gives, someone waits, and the rules of distribution are not written down.

## The standing figure holds both scales and coins

The central figure wears a red cap and outer garment over a blue-and-white striped robe. One hand holds a small balance; the other drops coins toward the person below on the left. Two people in patched garments kneel and reach toward the central figure. The covering on the left is yellowish, the one on the right blue.

Six large pentacles float above: three on the left, one in the middle and two on the right. Their pictorial placement differs from that of the small falling coins. Trees and buildings appear in the distance. The scales introduce the act of weighing, but do not by themselves prove fairness; the picture does not say how much the person on the right will receive next. [View the card image](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Pents06.jpg)

## Waite emphasises gifts and goodwill

Waite describes the central figure as a merchant and reads the distribution as evidence of success and a good heart. His meanings include presents, gifts, gratification and present prosperity. Reversed, he lists desire, greed, envy and illusion.

This article retains giving and receiving while adding modern questions about rules, respect and differences in power. These extend reflection on the pictured relationship. They should not be presented as evidence that Waite himself criticised the giver's motives. [Check Waite’s text](https://original.sacred-texts.com/tarot/pkt/pktpe06.htm)

## Upright Make help genuinely usable

There are two positions from which to approach this card. If you have capacity to help, first ask what is actually needed, then say how much you can provide and for how long. If you need help, you can accept support with clear limits without immediately trying to repay everything to remove your discomfort.

Useful help leaves room for the recipient's views. One act of support should not automatically buy lasting authority, and gifts should be distinguished from loans in advance. Discussing terms need not diminish goodwill; it can prevent later misunderstanding.

## Reversed Check the unspoken exchange

Imbalance sometimes hides inside “I only want what is best for you”: a little help becomes a demand for constant obedience, or someone keeps giving beyond their capacity in order to feel needed. Examine the actual arrangement before deciding how to change it.

You may also habitually refuse all help because accepting seems to create an unpayable debt. Check the person's actual expectations. Distinguish support whose terms can be discussed from help that genuinely carries controlling conditions.

## Look at distribution in everyday relationships

When allocating equipment or training places at work, explain the criteria and application process so resources do not only reach the most vocal people. If a friend helps edit a piece of work, agree beforehand which part to review and how much time to spend.

In a shared home, when someone temporarily takes on more tasks, agree when to review the arrangement rather than letting temporary help quietly become a permanent obligation. The person receiving support should also take part in the discussion.

## Practice Clarify one offer of help

Choose support you are currently giving or receiving. Write down its content, duration, decision-making rights and expectations of return. If either person understands one of these differently, clarify it in a specific conversation instead of guessing at the debt involved.

## Common misreading

The Six of Pentacles does not guarantee a cash gift, nor can it establish that a helper is insincere. It invites you to check whether support is useful, its terms transparent and the recipient's dignity and choices preserved.

## Sources and image

The image was drawn by Pamela Colman Smith. The source manuscript was based on inspection of the current original JPEG file; version details come from the [Commons file page](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Pents06.jpg).

The historical discussion follows [this card’s English entry](https://original.sacred-texts.com/tarot/pkt/pktpe06.htm) in Part III, Section 2 of A. E. Waite’s The Pictorial Key to the Tarot. The source is the English transcription labelled [1911] by the Internet Sacred Text Archive. A physical 1910 first edition was not checked for this batch. The everyday situations, questions and exercises are original modern reflections, not direct translations of Waite’s book.

sourceRecord.title: 星币六 给予也需要清楚的尺度
sourceRecord.oneLiner: 让资源流向需要的地方，并看清分配由谁决定。
sourceRecord.uprightQuickTake: 可提供或接受实际支持，把用途与边界说清。
sourceRecord.reversedQuickTake: 帮助附带隐形条件，或付出与决定权长期失衡。
sourceRecord.hook: 星币六有两只伸出的手，也有一架握在另一人手中的秤。它让我们同时看见善意和位置差异：有人在给，有人在等，分配的规则却未写出来。

sections.title: 秤和硬币都在站立者手中
paragraphs: 画面中央的人戴红帽、披红色外衣，内穿蓝白条纹衣袍。一手提着小天平，另一手向左下方的人撒下几枚小钱币。两名披着打补丁衣物的人跪在地上，伸手朝向中央人物；左侧披布偏黄，右侧偏蓝。
六枚大星币悬在人物上方，左边三枚，中间一枚，右边两枚，和正在落下的小钱币不是同一层次的画法。远处有树木和建筑。秤让“衡量”进入场景，但它并不能独自证明分配公平；画面也没有说明右边的人下一刻会得到多少。 [查看本篇牌面](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Pents06.jpg)

sections.title: Waite 强调馈赠与善意
paragraphs: Waite 将中央人物描述为商人，认为分发钱币反映他的成功与善心。占卜词条包括礼物、馈赠、满足以及当下的富足；逆位则包含欲求、贪求、嫉妒与幻象。
本篇保留给予和接受的主题，同时提出规则、尊重与权力差异的现代问题。这些是对画面关系的进一步反思，不能倒过来说 Waite 已经批判了图中施予者的动机。 [核对 Waite 原文](https://original.sacred-texts.com/tarot/pkt/pktpe06.htm)

sections.title: 正位 让帮助能够真正使用
paragraphs: 正位可以从两个位置进入。如果你有余力，先询问对方实际需要什么，再说明自己能提供多少、持续多久。如果你需要帮助，也可以接受一项边界清楚的支持，不必立刻用等量回报消除所有不安。
有效帮助允许接收者表达意见。一次性支援不应自动换来长期决定权，赠与和借用也应事先讲清。讨论这些条件不会让善意变少，反而能减少之后的误会。

sections.title: 逆位 检查没说出口的交换
paragraphs: 有些失衡藏在“我都是为你好”里：提供一点帮助，就要求对方随时服从；或为了维持被需要的感觉，持续承担自己已经无力承担的事。先看实际安排，再判断如何调整。
也可能是你习惯拒绝所有支持，认为接受就等于欠下无法偿还的人情。核实对方真实的期待，区分可以协商的帮助与确实附带控制的条件，不必把两者混在一起。

sections.title: 在三种日常关系中看分配
paragraphs: 团队分配设备或培训名额时，说明标准与申请方式，免得资源只流向最会开口的人。朋友帮忙改作品，可以事先约定看哪一部分、花多长时间。
共同生活中，某人暂时承担更多事务时，约好何时复盘，而不是让临时安排悄悄变成永久责任。被照顾的一方也应参与讨论。

sections.title: 练习 看清一项帮助的条件
paragraphs: 选一项正在给予或接受的支持，写下内容、期限、决定权和对回报的期待。若其中有一项双方理解不同，先用一次具体对话补齐，不要靠猜测计算人情。

sections.title: 容易看错的地方
paragraphs: 星币六不保证有人送钱，也不能凭牌面断定帮助者虚伪。它邀请你检查支持是否合用、条件是否透明，以及接受帮助的人是否仍保有尊严与选择。
